assessment.overall_rationale: The replicate sets strongly reproduce the canonical tip-cell module and the TGF-β-dependent CNS vascular module, while the left mechanosensory ion-channel module has no corresponding right-side program.

pair_scores.rationale: Both modules describe Nrp1–CDC42-dependent tip-cell identity, filopodial guidance, and sprouting supported by Angpt2, Cxcr4, and Cdc42ep3.
Both concern postnatal brain sprouting and share CXCR4, HOPX, Nrp1, and Tek, but the right module emphasizes Notch-linked arterial specification rather than tip-cell filopodia.
The modules overlap through Angpt2, Nrp1, and postnatal CNS angiogenesis, but tip-cell migration and TGF-β-dependent vascular integrity are distinct central mechanisms and outputs.
Both specify CNS endothelial tip behavior involving Nrp1, but the left module centers ALK5/TGF-β-dependent D-tip identity whereas the right centers CDC42-mediated filopodia.
Both link TGF-β/Nrp1 signaling to CNS sprouting-state specification, but the right module primarily asserts a Dll4-Notch-CXCR4 transition toward arterial fate.
Both center required Tgfbr1/2 signaling, regulated Angpt2, and deep postnatal brain vascular development, with D-tip specification versus integrity and remodeling as related output emphases.
The only overlap is the postnatal brain endothelial context, as ion-channel mechanosensing and neurovascular coupling are mechanistically distinct from angiogenic tip-cell filopodia.
Both occur in developing brain endothelium, but membrane ion-channel mechanosensing is peripheral to Notch-CXCR4-driven sprouting and arterial specification.
Brain vascular context is shared, but mechanosensory calcium signaling and TGF-β/Angpt2-dependent vascular integrity have different mechanisms and predicted phenotypes.
